en.title: Chronicles: Medieval IP Acquired by Coffee Stain After Developer Bankruptcy
en.summary: A surprising turn of events sees the ambitious medieval sandbox strategy game find a new home. Despite its developer declaring bankruptcy, development is set to continue under new ownership.
en.body:
In a dramatic turn of events that sent shockwaves through the gaming community, **Chronicles: Medieval** has a second chance at life. The ambitious historical sandbox strategy game, developed by **Raw Power Games**, was on the brink of disappearing entirely when its funding vanished overnight. The situation escalated rapidly, with **Raw Power Games** officially declaring bankruptcy on October 30, 2026, the very same day they announced their dire financial straits.

This sudden collapse put the future of **Chronicles: Medieval**, a title that had already garnered significant attention and wishlists on Steam, in serious jeopardy. However, a lifeline has been thrown by none other than **Coffee Stain**, the Swedish publisher known for hits like **Satisfactory** and **Deep Rock Galactic**. In a decisive move, **Coffee Stain** swooped in during the bankruptcy proceedings, acquiring the intellectual property and related assets for **Chronicles: Medieval** for approximately $5.42 million (36.75 million Danish Krone).

## A New Dawn for a Medieval Dream

The acquisition is structured in a way that ensures the original vision for **Chronicles: Medieval** can be realized. **Coffee Stain** has established a new company, of which they will own 75%. The remaining 25% will be held by a small group of key members from the original **Raw Power Games** development team. This ensures that the passion and expertise behind the game remain at its core, while the financial stability and publishing power of **Coffee Stain** provide the necessary support to move forward.

> "Chronicles: Medieval made a strong impression at its reveal at Summer Game Fest last year. We're happy to step in and help bring it to players after the recent developments in Copenhagen."

This statement from **Coffee Stain** CEO **Anton Westbergh** underscores their belief in the game's potential. The swift action taken by **Coffee Stain** demonstrates a commitment not just to acquiring an IP, but to fostering its completion and success. The game's strong performance on Steam wishlists, even outranking major upcoming titles, clearly signaled its appeal to a broad audience of both hardcore and casual gamers.

## What This Means for Players

For fans eagerly awaiting the chance to dive into the intricate world of **Chronicles: Medieval**, this news is a massive relief. The game, which was at one point described as being at "real risk of closing," is now back on track. The immediate concern for players was whether the game would ever see the light of day after the devastating news of **Raw Power Games**' bankruptcy. The involvement of key original developers in the new venture should also reassure players that the game's core identity will be preserved.

This situation serves as a stark reminder of the precarious nature of game development funding, particularly for ambitious independent projects. However, it also highlights the power of a compelling game concept to attract investment and support, even in the face of extreme adversity. The community's strong support, evidenced by its high wishlist ranking, undoubtedly played a role in **Coffee Stain**'s decision to invest.

## The Road Ahead

**Coffee Stain** has stated that their immediate focus is on working with the new company's management team to determine the best path forward for completing **Chronicles: Medieval**. While specific development timelines are still being finalized, the game is now slated for a Steam Early Access launch in early 2027, with console versions planned for release at a later date. This new chapter promises a brighter future for a game that almost vanished before it truly began.

content_raw: In late October, Chronicles: Medieval developer Raw Power Games announced that it was in trouble . Funding for its ambitious, historical sandbox strategy had suddenly been pulled, and as a result the studio was at "real risk of closing". But it turns out the situation was even more dire than the announcement suggested, as Raw Power Games declared bankruptcy on the same day. Despite this, development of Chronicles: Medieval will continue with at least some of its original creators involved, after Satisfactory developers Coffee Stain swooped in to purchase the assets and IP. In a press release , Coffee Stain said that it submitted the winning bid in Raw Power's sale process following the company's bankruptcy, paying 36.75 million Danish Krone (around $5.42 million) for Chronicles: Medieval's intellectual property. Rather than acquire the assets directly, however, Coffee Stain will transfer them directly to a "newly established company" that is owned 75% by Coffee Stain, and 25% by "a small group of key members of the game's original development team." Alongside paying full purchase price for Chronicles: Medieval's assets, Coffee Stain will also fund the continued development of the game. In a statement, Coffee Stain CEO Anton Westbergh said that "Chronicles: Medieval made a strong impression at its reveal at Summer Game Fest last year. We're happy to step in and help bring it to players after the recent developments in Copenhagen." He also explained that "Things have been moving fast around this deal, and our short-term focus will be on working out how best to complete the game, together with the new company's management team." Chronicles: Medieval is in the top 30 most wishlisted games on Steam, higher than the likes of Guild Wars 3 , Atomic Heart 2 , and the upcoming Mass Effect -like Exodus , so it's clear why this was an attractive proposition for Coffee Stain. What isn't clear from all this is how this affects Raw Power's existing staff. Presumably, Coffee Stain will seek to transfer as many people from Raw Power as they can, given they've been working on the game for years and therefore understand it intimately. But there's nothing in Coffee Stain's statement that confirms this. According to its Steam page, Chronicles: Medieval is still slated for an early access release in 2027, but it isn't clear at this juncture whether the acquisition will affect this.
